title: Pick the right evaluator
intro: Eight evaluation needs — match each to the cheapest tier that can actually answer it.

cards.text: Discard the worst 80% of 10,000 candidates, cheaply and deterministically
A quick first-pass alignment score between prompt and image
"Tell me WHY this mockup fails the brand guide, with feedback I can act on"
Score aesthetics and coherence across five dimensions with reasoning
"Is the cat actually to the RIGHT of the flower?" — element by element
Compare 50 images fairly using the identical question set
Judge whether the ad reads respectfully in a culture you don't know
The final safety sign-off before a global campaign ships

debrief: The funnel logic: metrics are for volume (fast, deterministic, one number — no why); LLM judges are for explanations (multi-dimensional scores with actionable feedback); rubrics are for interpretability and fairness (same decomposed questions across every candidate); humans are for what automation genuinely can't judge — nuance, culture, safety. The discipline is using the *cheapest tier that answers the question*, and never skipping straight to humans.
